## BabelDOC: Lossless Formatting, Massive Volume

BabelDOC is a new generation of intelligent PDF translation tools, using advanced typesetting preservation technology to provide you with a professional-level bilingual translation experience. Whether it's cutting-edge academic papers or business analysis reports, BabelDOC helps you easily overcome language barriers while perfectly presenting the exquisite typesetting of the original document.

BabelDOC is now officially open source, hosted on [GitHub](https://github.com/funstory-ai/BabelDOC). Welcome to visit the project repository, give us a Star, and support this open source project together!

### Accurate bilingual comparison, authentic presentation

Using intelligent layout analysis technology, it accurately recognizes document structure and paragraph layout. The translation is aligned with the original text, allowing you to compare instantly while reading, greatly improving reading efficiency and understanding accuracy.

![](https://app.immersivetranslate.com/app-assets/img/babel-doc-bilingual-ff34efbe.png)

### Intelligent formula and text typesetting

Using formula recognition technology, it perfectly handles the complex typesetting scenarios of mathematical formulas and text. The formula content is preserved as is, and the text part is intelligently translated, ensuring the professionalism and accuracy of academic literature.

![](https://app.immersivetranslate.com/app-assets/img/babel-doc-fomula-ca5abf75.png)

### Native style perfectly presented

Using advanced style mapping technology, it fully retains the design elements of the original document such as fonts, colors, and spacing. It supports professional typesetting features such as hanging punctuation and adaptive zooming, ensuring that the translated document still maintains the original exquisite aesthetic.

![](https://app.immersivetranslate.com/app-assets/img/babel-doc-style-4970833b.png)

### Intelligent processing of complex typesetting

Using deep learning layout analysis technology, it easily handles complex typesetting forms such as multi-column layouts, tables, and lists. No matter how complex the document structure is, it can accurately recognize and optimize the translation to perfectly restore the original layout.

![](https://app.immersivetranslate.com/app-assets/img/babel-doc-typesetting-c5dc4d8c.png)

## Common Problems

How to use BabelDOC to translate PDFs in Zotero?

You can visit the [Zotero Immersive Translate Plugin](https://github.com/immersive-translate/zotero-immersivetranslate) repository and install the plugin using the README documentation. (Currently only available to Pro members)

Best application scenarios

1. Academic paper translation: journal papers, conference papers, research reports, etc.
2. E-books: books, technical manuals, etc. (with a low proportion of tables)

Scenarios not suitable for use

1. Scanned PDFs: including OCR processed documents
2. Academic submissions: not recommended for direct use in paper submissions

Translation services used

All users currently have access to the GLM-4-Flash-250414 model for translation, while Pro users can also choose to use the Qwen3.5-Plus/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/doubao-seed-2-0-lite/GPT-5-mini/Gemini-3-Flash/Kimi+Qwen/Kimi+DeepSeek/GLM-4.7 models for translation, subject to actual availability.

After comparison, we found that Kimi-K2.5 is effective in extracting terminology, hence we are introducing the "Kimi + Qwen" and "Kimi + DeepSeek" translation services:

If you choose the "Kimi + Qwen" translation service and enable automatic terminology extraction, Kimi-K2.5 will be used to extract terminology, and Qwen3.5-Plus will be used to complete the text translation. All related consumption will be counted towards Qwen usage. (Limited time test)

If you choose the "Kimi + DeepSeek" translation service and enable automatic terminology extraction, Kimi-K2.5 will be used to extract terminology, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash will be used to complete the text translation. All related consumption will be counted towards DeepSeek usage. (Limited time test)

Since BabelDOC uses a backend translation architecture, all translation logic is executed on the server side, independent of the translation engine used by the plugin. Therefore, the range of translation engines available for BabelDOC differs from those available for immersive translation plugins, and BabelDOC only supports certain advanced translation models, not all advanced models are available.

Technical advantages of BabelDOC

BabelDOC has the following core advantages in the field of PDF translation:

1. **Accurate typesetting restoration**: Unique layout analysis technology that fully retains the typesetting details of the original document, including fonts, colors, spacing, etc.
2. **Intelligent formula processing**: Advanced formula recognition technology that ensures perfect mixing of mathematical formulas and text
3. **Professional field optimization**: Specially optimized for professional documents such as academic papers to provide more accurate translation effects

Translation Quota Explanation

We currently use a "translation quota" based billing method, detailed as follows:

- Translation quotas are charged based on the number of **Tokens** used during the translation process.
- The **GLM-4-Flash-250414** model is available to all users, and every BabelDOC user receives a monthly quota of 500,000 Tokens for free model translations within BabelDOC. (Actual availability depends on the supply from upstream suppliers, and quotas are dynamically adjusted based on server load)
- Models such as **Qwen3.5-Plus/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/doubao-seed-2-0-lite/GPT-5-mini/Gemini-3-Flash/Kimi+Qwen/Kimi+DeepSeek/GLM-4.7** are exclusively for **Pro/Max** members, counted towards the members' general translation quota. Pro members enjoy up to **20 million Tokens** per month, while Max members can enjoy up to **50 million Tokens** per month. Failed translations are not counted towards the translation quota.

At the start of a translation task, the system will deduct the general translation quota in advance based on the calculation of "3000 Tokens × number of pages". Once the translation is complete, we will settle based on actual consumption, refunding any excess to your account, or requiring additional if insufficient. If any system errors occur during the translation, all deducted general translation quotas will be fully refunded to your account. When the automatic term extraction feature is not enabled, the deduction per page is 3000 Tokens/page. When the automatic term extraction feature is enabled, the deduction per page is 6000 Tokens/page.

From actual usage statistics, when automatic term extraction is enabled, the average consumption is about 7381.56 Tokens per page, with the P25–P75 range being 4215.42–9490.89 Tokens; when automatic term extraction is disabled, the average consumption is about 4702.98 Tokens per page, with the P25–P75 range being 2642.38–5797.40 Tokens. Here, P25 (the 25th percentile) indicates that 25% of the pages consume fewer Tokens than this value, and P75 (the 75th percentile) indicates that 75% of the pages consume fewer Tokens than this value. The P25–P75 range is used to describe the common consumption range for most pages, thereby reducing the impact of extreme samples on the overall assessment.

Translation performance explanation

BabelDOC uses parallel processing technology, and processing speed varies depending on document characteristics:

\- Documents around 50 pages: usually completed in 1-5 minutes
\- Documents around 500 pages: about 10-20 minutes to complete
\- Documents around 1000 pages: about 10-20 minutes to complete
\- Documents around 5000 pages: about 1-2 hours to complete
\- Processing time is affected by document complexity, server load, and other factors.

To ensure translation quality, we perform multiple optimization processes on each paragraph, including format analysis, text extraction, and translation optimization.

Concurrent Task Count Description

Single File Translation: When using the "Single File" translation feature, the system only supports one translation task at a time.

Batch Translation (Exclusive for Pro Members): Pro members can enjoy the batch translation feature, which allows up to 100 translation tasks to be queued simultaneously (limited-time test). Although the processing priority of batch translation tasks is lower than that of single file translations, this feature enables you to submit and translate a large number of files at once, enhancing work efficiency.

During peak periods of high system load, we prioritize the processing speed of single file translation tasks for Pro members to ensure a better user experience. The counts of single file translation and batch translation tasks are calculated independently.

Regarding the Retention Period of Translation Records

We will keep your translation records and related documents free of charge for 14 days.

After 14 days, your translation records and documents may be automatically deleted due to system cache clearing and other reasons, and cannot be recovered. Please save or download the necessary files within the validity period to avoid inconvenience.

Document limitation explanation

- Free users have a single translation limit of **166** pages, while Pro members can translate up to **5000** pages at a time
- If the page limit is exceeded, you can manually select the translation range (e.g., pages 1-100)

Usage tips

1. **Bilingual comparison display:** Set the PDF reader to double-page display mode to achieve bilingual comparison reading
2. **Translation Progress Explanation:** When generating a PDF file, font subsetting and drawing instruction optimization will be performed, which may take a long time. Please wait patiently
3. **Best practice:** It is recommended to test with a small document first, and become familiar with the tool's features before processing large documents

Known limitations

The current version has the following limitations, which we are actively optimizing:

01. Some formula sections may overlap.
02. Italicized text in translations will disappear.
03. Small sections (such as author information, citations, table of contents entries, etc.) may not be accurately recognized.
04. Only supports languages written in Latin, Chinese, Japanese, or Korean scripts as the source language.
05. Does not support documents with Vietnamese as the source language.
06. Does not support underlining.
07. Does not support translation of chart areas.
08. Does not support drop caps.
09. Does not support PDF Outline translation.
10. Does not support scanned, image-based, or OCR-based PDFs.
11. Does not support ligatures.
12. Does not support blueprints.
13. Does not support Type3 fonts.
14. Does not support image format inline formulas.
15. Does not support right-to-left formatted documents.
16. Only supports horizontally aligned text.
17. Currently, selective ignoring of translation areas is not supported (the system will default to ignoring the translation of reference areas)

What is the difference between BabelDOC and immersive translation's existing PDF translation

The main differences between BabelDOC and immersive translation in PDF processing are:

1. **Typesetting retention:** BabelDOC focuses on fully retaining the typesetting of the original document, including details such as fonts, colors, and spacing, rather than reformatting.
2. **Formula mixed typesetting support:** BabelDOC can intelligently process mixed typesetting of mathematical formulas, ensuring the mixing effect of formulas and text.
3. **Professional field support:** Specially optimized for the translation effects of professional documents such as academic papers.

Translation effect is not as expected

BabelDOC is still in the early development stage, and the translation effect may not be as expected. We are working hard to improve. If you encounter a problem, please use the feedback button on the top right of the translation result page to report it, and we will improve it as soon as possible.

Why is exporting PDF slow

Because when exporting a PDF at the end, it is necessary to perform drawing instruction cleanup, which consumes a lot of time, so there will be a lag. Please be patient.

When is it necessary to enable compatibility mode?

When compatibility mode is not enabled and the following issues occur in the translation, you need to enable compatibility mode:

1. Colored blocks turn black and affect reading
2. The entire page of text suddenly disappears
3. Each character in parts of the document has a space in between

What is the impact of enabling compatibility mode?

After enabling compatibility mode, BabelDOC will disable rich text translation, skip font subsetting, document cleanup, and drawing instruction optimization steps, resulting in increased file size.

Why are the translations and the original text overlapping in the translated file

This is because the original file is a scanned PDF after OCR processing. You can try enabling the OCR temporary solution and retry (only supports white background with black text PDFs).

When is it necessary to enable the OCR version temporary solution?

When your scanned/image PDF file has been OCR processed and has white background with black text, you can try enabling the OCR temporary solution. This solution will add white rectangular blocks below the translation to cover the original text content.

Why doesn't BabelDOC support custom APIs?

1. Security Risk: BabelDOC uses a backend translation architecture, and if custom APIs are allowed, users must submit their API Key to the backend. This not only involves key security issues but also risks malicious attacks (such as DDoS) due to the exposure of backend server IPs, severely affecting service stability.
2. Network Uncertainty: The backend needs to actively access the API provided by the user, which may cause the overall translation process to be abnormal due to network delays, cross-regional access failures, or unstable intermediate links.
3. Uncontrollable Performance: BabelDOC's backend may issue hundreds of concurrent requests per second. We cannot predict the processing capacity of user APIs, and if the concurrency capacity is low, it will directly affect the overall translation speed and stability.
4. Disproportionate Resource Costs: If delays occur due to insufficient performance of user-customized APIs, the system will need to allocate additional computing resources for compensation. This will lead to resource wastage, and there is currently no reasonable way to account for costs and share charges.
5. High Architectural Complexity: If custom APIs are called via frontend relay, it will introduce more network hops and reliability challenges, and have a significant negative impact on performance, stability, and user experience.

In conclusion, BabelDOC will not support the integration of custom APIs at this stage. Our current focus is on continuously improving the translation quality and stability of BabelDOC. In the future, as the system matures, we will further explore and evaluate more flexible business models and possibilities for functional expansion.

When using split translation, only the first part performs detection if not skipped. - `--ocr-workaround`: Use OCR workaround (default: False). Only suitable for documents with black text on white background. When enabled, white rectangular blocks will be added below the translation to cover the original text content, and all text will be forced to black color. - `--auto-enable-ocr-workaround`: Enable automatic OCR workaround (default: False). See "Important Interaction Note" below for crucial details on how this interacts with `--ocr-workaround` and `--skip-scanned-detection`. - `--primary-font-family`: Override primary font family for translated text. If not specified, uses automatic font selection based on original text properties. - `--only-include-translated-page`: Only include translated pages in the output PDF. This option is only effective when `--pages` is used. (default: False) - `--merge-alternating-line-numbers`: Enable post-processing to merge alternating line-number layouts (keep the number paragraph as an independent paragraph b; merge adjacent text paragraphs a and c across it when `layout_id` and `xobj_id` match, digits are ASCII and spaces only). This skips all translation-related processing including layout analysis, paragraph finding, style processing, and translation itself. Useful for testing PDF parsing and reconstruction functionality. - `--remove-non-formula-lines`: Remove non-formula lines from paragraph areas (default: False). This removes decorative lines that are not part of formulas, while protecting lines in figure/table areas. Useful for cleaning up documents with decorative elements that interfere with text flow. - `--non-formula-line-iou-threshold`: IoU threshold for detecting paragraph overlap when removing non-formula lines (default: 0.9). Higher values are more conservative and will remove fewer lines. - `--figure-table-protection-threshold`: IoU threshold for protecting lines in figure/table areas when removing non-formula lines (default: 0.9). Normalization involves lowercasing and replacing hyphens (`-`) with underscores (`_`). - If `tgt_lng` is omitted for an entry, that entry is considered applicable for any `--lang-out`. - The name of each glossary (used in LLM prompts) is derived from its filename (without the .csv extension). - During translation, the system will check the input text against the loaded glossaries. If terms from a glossary are found in the current text segment, that glossary (with the relevant terms) will be included in the prompt to the language model, along with an instruction to adhere to it. ### Output Control [Permalink: Output Control](https://github.com/funstory-ai/BabelDOC#output-control) - `--output`, `-o`: Output directory for translated files. This creates a zip file containing all required models and fonts. - `--restore-offline-assets`: Restore an offline assets package from the specified file. This extracts models and fonts from a previously generated package. Tip 1. Offline assets packages are useful for environments without internet access or to speed up installation on multiple machines. 2. Generate a package once with `babeldoc --generate-offline-assets /path/to/output/dir` and then distribute it. 3. Restore the package on target machines with `babeldoc --restore-offline-assets /path/to/offline_assets_*.zip`. 4. The offline assets package name cannot be modified because the file list hash is encoded in the name. 5. If you provide a directory path to `--restore-offline-assets`, the tool will automatically look for the correct offline assets package file in that directory. 6. The package contains all necessary fonts and models required for document processing, ensuring consistent results across different environments. 7. The integrity of all assets is verified using SHA3-256 hashes during both packaging and restoration. 8. Warning **All APIs of BabelDOC should be considered as internal APIs, and any direct use of BabelDOC is not supported.** ## Background [Permalink: Background](https://github.com/funstory-ai/BabelDOC#background) There are a lot projects and teams working on to make document editing and translating easier like: - [mathpix](https://mathpix.com/) - [Doc2X](https://doc2x.noedgeai.com/) - [minerU](https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU) - [PDFMathTranslate](https://github.com/PDFMathTranslate/PDFMathTranslate) There are also some solutions to solve specific parts of the problem like: - [layoutreader](https://github.com/microsoft/unilm/tree/master/layoutreader): the read order of the text block in a pdf - [Surya](https://github.com/surya-is/surya): the structure of the pdf This project hopes to promote a standard pipeline and interface to solve the problem. In fact, there are two main stages of a PDF parser or translator: - **Parsing**: A stage of parsing means to get the structure of the pdf such as text blocks, images, tables, etc. - **Rendering**: A stage of rendering means to render the structure into a new pdf or other format. For a service like mathpix, it will parse the pdf into a structure may be in a XML format, and then render them using a single column reader order as [layoutreader](https://github.com/microsoft/unilm/tree/master/layoutreader) does. The bad news is that the original structure lost. Some people will use Adobe PDF Parser because it will generate a Word document and it keeps the original structure. But it is somewhat expensive. And you know, a pdf or word document is not a good format for reading in mobile devices. We offer an intermediate representation of the results from parser and can be rendered into a new pdf or other format. The pipeline is also a plugin-based system which everybody can add their new model, ocr, renderer, etc. ## Roadmap [Permalink: Roadmap](https://github.com/funstory-ai/BabelDOC#roadmap) - [ ] Add line support - [ ] Add table support - [ ] Add cross-page/cross-column paragraph support - [ ] More advanced typesetting features - [ ] Outline support - [ ] ... # Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition **arXiv:2605.10845** (cs) \[Submitted on 11 May 2026\] # Title:BabelDOC: Better Layout-Preserving PDF Translation via Intermediate Representation Authors: [Qi Yang](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Yang,+Q), [Xiangyao Ma](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Ma,+X), [Xiao Wang](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Wang,+X), [Hao Wang](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Wang,+H), [Rui Wang](https://arxiv.org/search/cs?searchtype=author&query=Wang,+R) View a PDF of the paper titled BabelDOC: Better Layout-Preserving PDF Translation via Intermediate Representation, by Qi Yang and 4 other authors [View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.10845) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.10845v1) > Abstract:As global cross-lingual communication intensifies, language barriers in visually rich documents such as PDFs remain a practical bottleneck. Existing document translation pipelines face a tension between linguistic processing and layout preservation: text-oriented Computer-Assisted Translation (CAT) systems often discard structural metadata, while document parsers focus on extraction and do not support faithful re-rendering after translation. We introduce BabelDOC, an Intermediate Representation (IR)-based framework for layout-preserving PDF translation. BabelDOC decouples visual layout metadata from semantic content, enabling document-level translation operations such as terminology extraction, cross-page context handling, glossary-constrained generation, and formula placeholdering. The translated content is then re-anchored to the original layout through an adaptive typesetting engine. Experiments on a curated 200-page benchmark, together with human evaluation and multimodal LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, show that BabelDOC improves layout fidelity, visual aesthetics, and terminology consistency over representative baselines, while maintaining competitive translation precision. The open-source toolkit and its interactive downstream applications are publicly available and have attracted over 8.4K GitHub stars and 17 contributors at the time of writing. # BabelDOC: The Revolutionary Open-Source PDF Translation Tool

![aibase](https://app.aibase.com/icon/logo.png)

#### AIbase基地

Published in [AI News](https://www.aibase.com/news) · 4min read · Apr 11, 2025

754

Recently, an open-source PDF translation tool named **BabelDOC** has been officially launched. Its powerful features and flexible configuration have quickly made it a focal point in the AI translation field. According to AIbase, BabelDOC not only preserves the original layout of PDF documents but also supports bilingual comparison, batch processing, and compatibility with various AI models, making it one of the best PDF translation solutions currently available. The release of this tool offers a new intelligent option for academic research, international communication, and multilingual document processing.

![image.png](https://upload.chinaz.com/2025/0411/6387996502107408109972926.png)

### Powerful Features: One-Click Bilingual PDF Generation

BabelDOC's core strength lies in its efficient translation capabilities. Users can generate bilingual PDFs with a single click, supporting side-by-side or alternating displays of the original and translated text, ensuring a smooth reading experience. Even more impressive is the tool's ability to accurately preserve the original formatting style. The translated document maintains a high degree of consistency with the original file in terms of font, spacing, and layout.

### Flexible Operation: Batch Processing and Accurate Translation

BabelDOC supports batch processing, allowing users to translate multiple PDF files simultaneously, ideal for large-scale document needs. The tool also allows users to specify page numbers for translation; simply select the pages to be translated to complete the task, avoiding unnecessary resource waste. **This design fully considers the actual needs of users**, demonstrating the tool's high practicality.

### Technological Innovation: Structure Awareness and Model Compatibility

The technical core of BabelDOC is its structure-aware translation capability. Using advanced algorithms, the tool can identify the complex structure of PDF documents, ensuring that the translation result matches the original layout. Furthermore, BabelDOC supports flexible LLM integration, compatible with OpenAI-like interfaces and local models like Ollama. Users can choose the appropriate model for translation based on their needs. **This multi-model support not only lowers the barrier to entry** but also provides more possibilities for translation needs in different scenarios.

### Open-Source Ecosystem: Self-Deployment and Extensibility

As an open-source tool, BabelDOC offers powerful self-deployment capabilities. It supports online use, command-line operation, self-deployment, and Python API access, meeting the diverse needs of individual users and enterprise developers. Its plugin-based architecture design facilitates functional expansion, allowing for easy integration of OCR, paragraph grouping, and other features in the future. **This open design will attract more developers to participate**, contributing to the continued growth of the BabelDOC ecosystem.
